parameters.name: VendorName
parameters.description: The vendor name of the SFP. When empty, the vendor name is not used in determining the SFP type.

parameters.name: VendorOUI
parameters.description: The vendor organizationally unique identifier (OUI) field of the SFP. When empty, the vendor OUI is not used in determining the SFP type.

parameters.name: VendorPN
parameters.description: The vendor part number (PN) of the SFP. When empty, the vendor PN is not used in determining the SFP type. The ASCII character `*` is interpreted as a wildcard character. Note: the string "*" as value for this parameter is equivalent to the empty string as value for this parameter.

parameters.name: SFPType
parameters.description: It has the same allowed values as {{param|##.SFPCage.{i}.SFPType}}, except for "Unsupported".

object.description: List of SFPs to help implementations to determine the SFP type. {{param|##.SFPCage.{i}.SFPType}} reports the SFP type. SFPs themselves do not report their type. Implementations typically try to determine a value for that parameter based on the values for parameters such as: - {{param|##.Mgmt.SFF8472.{i}.Transceiver.Transceiver}} - {{param|##.Mgmt.SFF8472.{i}.Transceiver.BRNominal}} - {{param|##.Mgmt.SFF8472.{i}.Transceiver.Wavelength}} This approach is not foolproof: many SFPs do not report correct values. They e.g. might report 0 as value for all transceiver codes. What all SFPs normally report correctly is their vendor name, vendor OUI and part number, cfr: - {{param|##.Mgmt.SFF8472.{i}.Transceiver.VendorName}} - {{param|##.Mgmt.SFF8472.{i}.Transceiver.VendorOUI}} - {{param|##.Mgmt.SFF8472.{i}.Transceiver.VendorPN}} Therefore this table specifies the SFP type based on vendor name, vendor OUI and/or part number. After reading those 3 properties, implementations can look up the value to assign to {{param|##.SFPCage.{i}.SFPType}} in this table. This list is allowed to include a built-in module/SFP to help an implementation to determine the type of such a module/SFP.
